meta.title: Boots and Bees in Green Hill

paragraphs: On Sunday, it rained in Green Hill until the morning. Lily and Tom put on their rubber boots. "Today we are going walking," said Grandpa. Pip ran in front of them, and his tail went up and down. The air was fresh, and it smelled like wet grass. They walked along a wet path between two green fields.

Soon they came to a big puddle. A puddle is a small pool of rain water on the road. "I will jump over it," said Tom. But his boot went into the water, and brown water jumped up. Pip jumped in, too, and he nearly fell over. Lily laughed, and she had brown water on her face. "Pip, you are very dirty!" she said.

They continued along the path, and they saw a strange man in a field. He did not move, and he wore an old hat. "Who is that man?" asked Lily. "That is a scarecrow," said Grandpa. "It is a man made of dry grass and old clothes, and it keeps birds away." Tom looked at the old hat and smiled. "Is that your hat, Grandpa?" he asked. "Yes, it is," said Grandpa, and he laughed.

At the end of the field, there were some white wooden boxes among the trees. "These are my hives," said Grandpa. "A hive is a house for bees." The hives were quiet, and Grandpa spoke softly. Only a few bees flew around, because the air was cool. "Every hive has one queen," said Grandpa. "She is bigger than the other bees, and she stays inside." "Can we see her?" asked Lily. "Not today," said Grandpa. "But we can look at the honey."

Grandpa took a small bottle from a box. The honey was gold and sweet. Then they walked home along the same path. Lily and Tom washed their boots in the garden. Grandma was in the kitchen, and she had warm bread on the table. They put honey on the bread, and everybody ate it. "A walk in the country is the best," said Tom. Pip slept under the table, and he was still dirty.
